recipes.name: Buttermilk Strawberry Shortcake
ingredients_raw: 0.75 cup chilled unsalted butter, cut into small pieces

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Whisk flour, baking powder, baking soda, 1/3 cup white sugar, and salt together in a mixing bowl.
Cut in cold butter with a knife or pastry blender until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Stir in buttermilk until the flour mixture is moistened.
Drop 1/3-cup scoops of the dough 2 inches apart onto the prepared baking sheet.
Brush biscuits with heavy cream and sprinkle generously with turbinado sugar.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden brown, 15 to 20 minutes.
Mix sliced strawberries, 1/4 cup white sugar, and lemon juice in a large bowl. Allow berries to rest until juices develop, about 30 minutes.
Serve strawberries with juice over the baked biscuits.

raw_recipe.headline: Buttermilk Strawberry Shortcake
raw_recipe.description: Light and airy buttermilk shortcake biscuits are topped with juicy, fresh strawberries in this easy recipe that makes a summer dessert favorite.

video.description: In this video, you’ll see how to make strawberry shortcake with buttermilk biscuits. Top the light and airy biscuits with fresh, juicy strawberries and whipped cream. The biscuits are super simple.

review.reviewBody: What a simple, easy, and delicious dessert! I had some buttermilk I had to use up and this was just perfect. For the shortcakes, I froze the butter and grated it which is much easier. After dropping these onto a baking sheet lined with parchment paper and did an egg wash (one egg well beaten with 1 Tbsp. of water) and then topped it off with the turbinado sugar which provided a nice little crunch. These baked up beautifully and tasted wonderful. I served them with "Easy Whipped Cream" from this site. This recipe is a definite keeper!

Great simple, easy and delicious recipe. I sliced some of the strawberries ahead of time in order for the juice to form. The only ingredient change I made was to sprinkle with light brown sugar instead of turbinado. A word of caution, watch the baking time. While the recipe does not require whipped cream, I did add it on the side. Going in my favorite recipe file. Thanks Emmie4life for sharing your recipe here on Allrecipes.

Recipe Group Selection: 19, May '12 ~ Oh my gosh, is this shortcake ever delicious! I usually make a shortcake similar to this, but not with the buttermilk. Really liked the texture the buttermilk added. I cut the recipe down to 3 shortcakes because I did not want leftovers. I used the heavy cream and course sugar crystals on top as I'm not sure what turbinado sugar is. It baked up nicely and was a soft and fluffy on the inside and golden brown and crunchy on the outside. I will make shortcake this way from now on as I usually always have buttermilk on hand. Really enjoyed this week's Recipe Group pick.

I made this recipe almost exactly as written (and tripled it for a large 4th of July party)- which yielded me 48 shortcake biscuits. Instead of brushing the top of the unbaked biscuits with heavy cream, I used an egg wash. I also baked them at 400 degrees. Also instead of dropping them by spoonfuls, I divided each recipe of the dough into 2 and patted them into circles and cut them into wedges-8 wedges per 1/2 half of the dough. They were delicious!!!!! Make sure you put the sugar on top of them, it makes a huge difference.

I made a half recipe (10 smaller servings) since I didn't want stale leftovers. I used muffin tins with canola spray and was able to shave a few minutes off the baking time. Using normal white sugar on top still worked fine. I used the suggestion of the food processor for adding the butter and will be doing that from now on - worked like a charm with cold butter from the fridge. These were more moist than other shortcakes I've made.
Great recipe! I grated the butter using the small holes of the box grater and substituted 1 cup plain yogurt for the buttermilk - very tasty!

I froze the butter and then used the mandolin's julianne attachment to cut it. 2% milk and 1 tsp vinegar as a sub for the buttermilk, and 2% and regular sugar for the topping. I used 2 lbs of strawberries. Yum!

I halved this recipe and let the strawberries sit for longer than 30 minutes. The shortcakes came out great, will definitely make again! I ended up combining the dry mixture with the butter by using cold (out of fridge) cubed butter and using a pastry cutter to getting it into crumbs. 

I also had some lemon curd lying around so I had some on the side with it and it was delicious!

This was my first attempt at shortcake and these turned out perfect! My family raved about how delicious they were. I made a few changes: didn't have buttermilk so mixed whole milk with 2TBS of vinegar and let it sour for a few mins. I added a tsp of vanilla extract (this is what really made them for me), and added about one extra tablespoon of sugar. They were so good that I made them the next day and added chocolate chips to them. Mmm!!!

Very simple to make. Nice clean classic taste. I made mine with King Arthur gluten free flour. I added an additional 1/2 tsp of baking powder and an extra pinch of baking soda to help the rise. I put a spring
I didn't have any buttermilk so I used 3/4 cup of 2% and 1/4 18% cream with about a tablespoon of vinegar to sour it. Excellent recipe!
Great roundup of buttermilk recipes! That dressing idea is going on my salad tonight.

Delicious!! The biscuit alone was worth the effort. It was sweet, light and easy to throw together. I’m using this recipe from now on!!! Btw I didn’t have turbinado. I used regular sugar. Good enough.
This recipe is a keeper! I made this for our small group and everyone loved it. It was easy to put together and turned out perfectly.
These biscuits were very good. I made the recipe as written, baked them on a pizza stone in a 400 degree oven for 16 minutes. That worked well for my oven.
These biscuits are so good! Light and just a little sweet.
The strawberries need way more juice. Mash half of them then add enough water to make enough juice for each shortcake. You may need to add more sugar.

This is the go to recipe every June when the strawberries come into season. The biscuits are the perfect complement to freshly harvested strawberries. Slice a biscuit in half, two spoonfuls of strawberries over the bottom half, a dollop of whipped cream, then the top half of the biscuit. Two more spoonfuls of strawberries and a second dollop of whipped cream to top it all off. Enjoy!

Easy & delicious! (Didn’t have buttermilk. Mixed 1 cup of 1/2 & 1/2 and 1 tbsp lemon juice to make my own). I brushed w 1/2 & 1/2 and lots of the turbinado sugar. The more bumps on the top the better, makes it crispy. I think this recipe would be great sugar and adding garlic, cheddar cheese and herbs, bake and then brush with a melted butter & garlic mix.
